content: Nutritional screening and assessment are critical components of medical practice, as nutrition plays a fundamental role in both health and disease management. Acute and chronic diseases affecting various organ systems can significantly impact food intake and metabolism, often leading to increased catabolism. This metabolic imbalance contributes to nutrition-related conditions that are associated with heightened morbidity and, in severe cases, mortality. Proper nutrition can delay or prevent the onset of disorders such as cardiovascular disease, diabetes, cancer, and cognitive decline. Malnutrition is defined as a state resulting from inadequate intake or absorption of nutrients, leading to altered body composition, specifically a reduction in fat-free mass and body cell mass. This condition results in diminished physical and mental function and adversely affects clinical outcomes in the context of disease. Life-threatening causes of malnutrition include conditions that, if left untreated, may result in death or irreversible disability within 24 hours.
